verdict.rationale: Twenty ships its own first-party app-development toolkit: a CLI scaffolder (`npx create-twenty-app`), objects, fields and views defined as code, a live-sync `dev` command, and publishing. That is an official build-against framework, alongside auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs. The evidence never names a packaged client SDK or language libraries, and the OpenAPI probe returned 404. Missing for 10: explicitly documented official client SDKs (e.g., TypeScript/Python packages) for calling the API, SDK reference docs, a published OpenAPI spec for generating clients, independent hands-on corroboration of the app toolkit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Scaffold a new app with the Twenty CLI: npx create-twenty-app my-app ... Define objects, fields, and views as code
`dev` | Watch source files and live-sync changes
Developers can build full-featured apps on top of Twenty — adding custom UI, server-side logic, and deep integrations.
Both GraphQL and REST endpoints, with auto-generated documentation per workspace.
